newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No cold in sight for Brazil coffee regions - Somar.
newsitem.headline: No cold in sight for Brazil coffee regions - Somar.

text.p: Brazil's coffee regions face no risk of frost over the coming days, with minimum temperatures expected to remain between 12 and 17 degrees Celsius, local meteorologists Somar said on Thursday.

Any polar air masses continue to remain blocked in the far south of the country, with the forecast for the next two days one of sun and stable temperatures for coffee areas, said Somar forecaster Marcos Massari.
A weak cold front will quickly pass through the coffee regions over the weekend increasing cloud cover but with no forecasts of rain, he added.

Massari attributed the milder weather over the past month after a cold snap at the beginning of June to the gradual development of the El Nino weather pattern which is being seen in warmer ocean temperatures in the Pacific.

"It seems as if the El Nino is beginning to have an effect already. If it wasn't for the El Nino, this would be a very cold winter as seen at the beginning of June. But it looks as if the El Nino may have saved coffee regions," he added.
